parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for a pure Rust 2021 Cargo project in /output, std-only parsing, root test5.rs, exact stdout formatting, no-argument exit behavior, and black-box inference from the executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although multi-agent mode was enabled and the agent mentioned splitting off probing, protocol validation and the ledger show zero spawned children; the parent owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and delivery.
parallel.implementation: The parent inferred permissive URL splitting rules through executable probes, wrote Cargo.toml, test5.rs, src/lib.rs, src/url_parser.rs, and submodules, then fixed a Rust module path error after failed builds.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final tree included both Cargo release artifacts and a standalone /output/test5 executable; artifact validation accepted the expected entry and supporting module files.
parallel.verification: It ran cargo build --release, rustc --edition=2021 test5.rs -O -o test5, cargo test, a byte-level URL matrix comparison, and a no-argument exit-code check before final response.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task obligation is visible at closure; the transient compile failure was corrected and the official evaluator passed all 40 testcases.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, Cargo, root test5.rs, exact-output, CLI-argument, and black-box executable probing requirements from the shared prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial run kept all work with the main actor, with multi-agent disabled and no child activity; the parent owned probing, implementation, verification, and final delivery.
serial.implementation: The parent probed a broad URL matrix, then wrote Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/port.rs, src/url.rs, and test5.rs with a different but compatible module layout.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The final tree contained the Cargo project, release binary, root executable copy, and parser library files, and artifact validation accepted the expected test5.rs entry.
serial.verification: It ran cargo test and cargo build --release, recovered from a rejected rm-based comparison command, reran parity checks successfully, checked no-argument exit parity, and tried unavailable formatters.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task obligation is visible at closure; formatter tooling was absent but nonblocking, and the official evaluator passed all 40 testcases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required Rust port, exact stdout behavior, std-only constraint, Cargo layout, root test5.rs, and black-box use of the executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same required Rust port, CLI behavior, std-only constraint, Cargo layout, root entry file, and black-box executable probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference; both implemented the same task obligations and official tests passed in both modes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel mode was configured for multi-agent use, but protocol validation reports zero spawn calls, child thread IDs, child agent paths, and child activity events.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial mode had multi-agent disabled and likewise no child activity, so the main actor owned the complete work sequence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The only decomposition difference is configuration: parallel had the capability enabled but did not actually delegate. Both runs were effectively single-owner attempts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel transferred no child briefs or handoffs; all task knowledge came from the prompt, local source viewing, and executable probe outputs consumed by the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial likewise had no child briefs or cross-agent handoffs, and the parent used local probe output to infer parser contracts before coding.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No cross-agent context boundary existed in either run, so no interface or handoff difference explains the outcome.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a Cargo package named test5_port with url_parser.rs plus authority and split submodules, initially hit module lookup errors, then patched path attributes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a Cargo package named test5 with src/url.rs and src/port.rs modules and did not show the same Rust module path compile failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementations had different file organization and transient local defects, but both converged on the required parser behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no child results to retrieve or join; the parent handled failed compile output, applied a fix, then consumed later successful build and test outputs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve or join; the parent handled a rejected comparison command by rerunning a safer comparison and then continued to final checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both result lifecycles were parent-local. Parallel had a compile-error/fix cycle, serial had a rejected-command/retry cycle, and neither involved cross-agent result loss.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel assembled a single accepted /output tree with Cargo.toml, test5.rs, parser modules, release binary, and root executable; no concurrent writer collision appears.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial assembled a single accepted /output tree with Cargo.toml, test5.rs, parser modules, release binary, and copied root executable; no shared-state collision appears.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The final tree layouts differed, but each had one owner and passed artifact validation, so there was no merge or shared-state disadvantage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran Cargo build, standalone rustc build, cargo test, a broad byte-level output comparison, and a no-argument exit parity check before finalizing; official evaluation passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran cargo test, cargo build --release, corrected the comparison command to get all matched, checked no-argument exit parity, and official evaluation passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Verification was materially sufficient in both runs. Parallel also compiled test5.rs directly, while serial attempted formatting but lacked formatter tooling.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed normally without timeout in 252.698 cell seconds after 220.34 agent seconds, under the 2400 second budget.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed normally without timeout in 284.601 cell seconds after 250.233 agent seconds, under the 2400 second budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No budget pressure or closure failure affected either run; parallel finished slightly faster but without actual concurrent execution.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official completed evaluations passed 40 of 40 testcases. The attempts differed in module layout and transient local problems, but neither produced a task-solving shortfall. The parallel run was configured for multi-agent mode but did not execute a child-agent mechanism, so no parallel coordination episode explains an outcome difference.
parallel_contributors: Single parent actor inferred parser behavior through black-box probes, wrote the Cargo project, fixed a module path error, and verified outputs before finalizing.
serial_contributors: Single parent actor inferred parser behavior through black-box probes, wrote a different Cargo layout, corrected a rejected verification command, and verified outputs before finalizing.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel initially placed submodules where Rust did not find them and patched path attributes after compile failures.
Serial used a different parser module split and encountered an environment/tooling issue for cargo fmt and rustfmt after verification was already complete.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; both independent attempts passed official evaluation
